candidates.name: Majorelle Gardens
candidates.price: 170 dirham, 30 dirham extra for the Berber Museum
candidates.content: It provides an excellent respite from the hustle and bustle of the city streets, if not crowded by tourists as it sometimes is. The park was designed by the artist Jacques Majorelle in the 1920s and 1930s. Since 1980 the garden ha

candidates.name: El Bahia Palace
candidates.price: Foreigners: adult 100 dirham, child aged 7–13 50 dirham; Moroccan/resident: adult 30 dirham, child aged 7–13 10 dirham
candidates.content: An ornate palace complex built in the late 19th century, with courtyards, gardens, richly decorated rooms and traditional Moroccan architectural details. The palace was begun in the 1860s by Si Moussa, grand vizier to Sultan Muham

candidates.name: El Badi Palace
candidates.price: Foreigners: adult 100 dirham, child aged 7–13 50 dirham; Moroccan/resident: adult 30 dirham, child aged 7–13 10 dirham
candidates.content: The palace complex is extensive, with ruins, courtyards, underground passages and exhibitions. The terrace offers views over the surrounding Medina and the Atlas Mountains on clear days. Allow around 45–90 minutes to explore the m

candidates.name: Koutoubia Mosque
candidates.content: Named after the booksellers market that used to be located here. It is said that the minaret of the Koutoubia mosque is to Marrakech as the Eiffel Tower is to Paris. The minaret is visible from Gueliz which is connected to the Med

candidates.name: Yves Saint Laurent Museum
candidates.price: 120 dirham, combination ticket with Majorelle Gardens and Berber Museum 180 dirham, queues are far shorter here than at the gardens to buy tickets though you have to buy either a YSL Museum ticket or combination ticket
candidates.content: Advance bookings must be made online, it is not possible to buy a ticket at the site.

candidates.name: Marrakech Museum
candidates.content: It's housed in the Dar Menebhi Palace, constructed at the end of the 19th century.

candidates.name: Saadian Tombs
candidates.price: Foreigners: adult 100 dirham, children aged 7–13 50 dirham; Moroccan nationals and residents: adult 30 dirham, child 10 dirham
candidates.hours: generally 09:00–17:00, although visitors should check current information before travelling
candidates.content: Saadian Tombs. The tombs were built in the 16th century as the dynastic necropolis of the Saadian dynasty. The complex includes the Chamber of the Twelve Columns, the Chamber of the Mihrab, the Chamber of the Three Niches and the

candidates.name: Ben Youssef Madrasa
candidates.price: Foreigners 50 dirham; Moroccans (with ID) 20 dirham; children under 12 10 dirham
candidates.hours: 09:00–19:00 daily (during Ramadan 09:00–16:30), closed for religious holidays
candidates.content: One of the largest madrassas in North Africa. It is a school attached to the Ben Youssef Mosque and is home to beautiful art and architecture. The present building was completed in 1564–1565 under the Saadian sultan Abdallah al-Gh

candidates.name: The Menara gardens
candidates.content: A mixture of orchards and olive groves surrounding the water reservoir with the central pavilion which is a popular sight on tourist postcards. Not a decorative garden, and now quite run down. The pavilion was built during the 16t

candidates.name: Slat Al Azama Synagogue
candidates.content: Synagogue which is not only a place of worship with a beautiful open courtyard, but also includes interesting displays about Judaism's varied history in Morocco, including photos of Jews in the Berber Mountains.

candidates.name: Agdal Gardens
candidates.content: It consists of groves of orange, lemon, fig, apricot and pomegranate trees in rectangular plots, linked by olive-lined walkways. Together with the medina of Marrakech and the Menara Gardens, the Agdal Gardens were listed by UNESCO

candidates.name: Djemaa El-Fna
candidates.content: The highlight of any Marrakech night. Musicians, dancers, and story tellers pack this square at the heart of the medina, filling it with a cacophony of drum beats and excited shouts. Scores of stalls sell a wide array of Moroccan

candidates.name: Dar Si Saïd Museum
candidates.price: Locals: adult 10 dirham, child below 12 3 dirham; tourists: adult 30 dirham
candidates.content: Museum set in an old palace with beautiful gardens. While somewhat run-down, it is worth seeing and houses many different artifacts from Morocco through the ages, such as wood carvings, musical instruments, and weapons. It is dedi

candidates.name: Ali Ben Youssef Mosque
candidates.content: The first mosque in Marrakesh was erected at this place by the Almoravid emir Yusuf ibn Tashfin in the 1070s. However, it was almost completely rebuilt in early 19th century by the Alaouite sultan Suleiman, with hardly any trace l

candidates.name: Medina
candidates.content: The Medina is the old city quarter located within the sandstone city walls that give Marrakech the nickname the Red City. As an ancient hub, it contains a maze of narrow streets and outdoor marketplaces.

candidates.name: The Souks
candidates.content: Markets of Marrakech, just adjacent to Place Djemaa El-Fna, are where you can buy almost anything, from spices to shoes, jellabas to kaftans, and tea pots to tagines. Undoubtedly, being a foreigner means you will end up paying hig

candidates.name: Moroccan Culinary Arts Museum
candidates.content: If you are interested in food and eating culture, you will enjoy this museum. Audiovisual information about the rich culinary culture of Marocco, its ingredients, techniques and traditions. You can also touch and smell many things

candidates.name: Maison de la Photographie
candidates.content: A little photography museum, it has one of the highest roof terraces in the Medina. Ticket is also valid for Museum of Mouassin Music.

candidates.name: Jewish Cemetery
candidates.content: The largest Jewish cemetery in Morocco, characterized by white-washed tombs and sandy graves. The men selling tickets are full of interesting information about the cemetery but you have to ask.

candidates.name: Musée de la Palmeraie
candidates.content: In old agricultural buildings in the Palmeraie, made out of rammed earth. The architecture itself is interesting if you haven't seen it. It offers a small collection of contemporary art, with a room dedicated to Moroccan artists (

candidates.name: Musee Farid Belkahia
candidates.content: A museum dedicated to the renowned contemporary artist Farid Belkahia, showcasing different periods of his work

candidates.name: Almoravid Koubba
candidates.content: A very small but intricate domed pavilion, known for being the only surviving example of Almoravid religious architecture (early 12th century) in Marrakech. Located across the street from the Ben Youssef Mosque, it is believed to

candidates.name: Tanneries
candidates.content: Visiting the tanneries can be an interesting experience. Even if some people tell you the area is only for locals, it is possible to visit the Tanneries without paying a youngster. After finding a tannery, ask one of the workers i

candidates.name: Moratra Medina walking tour
candidates.price: US$20 per person in a small group, US$60 per person private
candidates.content: A 2- to 4-hour walk through the old city with a licensed local guide, covering how the souks and their crafts are organised and landmarks such as the Bahia Palace, Ben Youssef Madrasa and the Saadian Tombs.

candidates.name: Les Bains de Marrakech
candidates.content: Tourists-oriented in good sense: couples can have hammam together in a private room. Extensive list of massages and spa treatments from 30 min to a full day. Reception and attendants are proficient in speaking English, however, th

candidates.name: Stade de Marrakesh
candidates.content: This is multi-use but mostly for football, with a capacity of 41,356. It's the home ground of Kawkab, who play in Botola 2 the second tier. In 2025 / 26 it hosted matches in the Africa Cup of Nations.

candidates.name: Chez Ali Fantasia
candidates.content: Horse show, acrobats on Arabian horses firing rifles in the air, horseback acrobatics, belly dancing, etc. It takes place at night in a huge imitation of an old castle.

candidates.name: Marrakech Paragliding
candidates.content: Leave the city behind and discover the incredible beauty of Morocco from above! Enjoy an exciting tandem paragliding experience near Marrakech, surrounded by the spectacular Atlas Mountains.

candidates.name: Thai marrakech
candidates.content: Bann Thai institute is a beauty center based in the heart of Marrakech. His team is a graduate of the famous school of Wat Po in Bangkok. The center offers several Thai massage relaxation with a traditional Moroccan hammam natural

candidates.name: Hamam Essalama
candidates.content: Friendly staff, however, no English or French (other locals helped without any problem)

candidates.name: Ô Bain de Lina
candidates.content: Friendly staff, however, no English or French; other customers likely to help you out.

candidates.name: Narwama
candidates.content: Restaurant and bar that has a fire fountain in the centre and an open roof around the patio. The atmosphere is very chilled and their food is very good, but slightly expensive. Good for pre-dinner drinks.

candidates.name: Chesterfield Pub
candidates.content: A slightly unusual experience, apparently an 'English pub' it serves Moroccan lager and has an outside pool in a courtyard with palm trees, not an entirely English experience. Much less touristy than it sounds with a mainly local

candidates.name: Le Salama
candidates.content: Happy hour from 17:00 until they close, mostly western pop classics on the top floor. Very touristy with shishas, belly dancing and waiters who wear a fez - none of it is typically Moroccan but the overall atmosphere is between re

candidates.name: Hotel Grand Tazi
candidates.content: The hotel has a public bar, serving beer and wine and is not overly expensive.

candidates.name: Montecristo
candidates.content: Nightclub with rooftop terrace

candidates.name: Jad Mahal
candidates.content: Lounge bar and formal restaurant.

candidates.name: Comptoir Darna
candidates.content: Cocktail bar and night club Dress code: elegant

candidates.name: African Chic
candidates.content: Moroccan Latin Brazilian. Also has a restaurant with a view to the dance floor.

candidates.name: Sky Lounge
candidates.content: Fashionable rooftop lounge on top of the Pearl Hotel

candidates.name: Chez Chegrouni
candidates.content: Their vegetarian couscous is supposedly the only true vegetarian couscous in town; it's also bland but they give you plenty of it. Prices go up if you sit on the terrace. Usually packed full of good-time tourists.

candidates.name: Henna Cafe
candidates.content: A pretty little cafe on 3 floors with an orange sign on the Berber hand-carved wooden facade opened in November 2011. You can have a cup of tea or coffee or simple lunch with dessert or just a sandwich. The Henna Café offers safe

candidates.name: Chez Yassine
candidates.content: Not much choice but served by very friendly people. Tajines and pizzas are great and you can also order skewers that are not on the menu.

candidates.name: Chez Bismilah
candidates.content: Amazing food and wonderful service. The owner is very kind and the fantastic chef is a humble lady who cooks perfectly all the traditional Moroccan recipes. Tayine Royale is recommended. The roof top has an amazing view over the o

candidates.name: Café Babouche medina
candidates.content: In a small street a few steps from the Jemaa El Fna square. You can eat there in a friendly atmosphere. The veal tagine with prunes and almonds is spectacular.

candidates.name: Black Pan
candidates.content: Italian restaurant. Artisanal pizzas, traditional Italian dishes and warm atmosphere.

candidates.name: Dar Yacout
candidates.content: Traditional Moroccan gastronomic cuisine. Has a terrace overlooking the Medina.

candidates.name: Les Jardins de la Medina
candidates.content: Traditional and modern Moroccan cuisine. Moroccan wine served by bottle and glass. Stylish restaurant with tall white columns.

candidates.name: Al Fassia
candidates.content: Traditional Moroccan food in cozy restaurant run by women (except the doorman). Wine served by the bottle.

candidates.name: La Villa des Orangers
candidates.price: 700 dirham for three-course menu. 500 dirham for a bottle of wine.
candidates.content: French gastronomic cuisine in a very calm and pleasant atmosphere. Enjoy your dinner in soft chairs, among dark woodpanels, bookcases and artwork. In the winter start with a drink at the fireplace.

candidates.name: Associacion Amal
candidates.hours: Lunch: daily 12:00-16:00, dinner: groups of min. 10 people by reservation only
candidates.content: Here you can experience lunch similar to what Moroccans eat at home: this women's aid association provides women with education in exchange for food which is then sold for financing the model.

candidates.name: Café Arabe
candidates.content: They have a Moroccan and an Italian cook, so there are two menus to choose from. There are three floors including the downstairs courtyard which is lovely for lunch. The top floor terrace has fantastic views, you can lounge on the
